title: Finite relative Tor dimension of a perfect tensor
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme], f:X -> S any scheme morphism, E a perfect object of D(O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex], and G a bounded complex of O_X-modules whose terms are flat over S [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then E tensor^L G [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] has finite Tor dimension over the inverse-image structure sheaf f^{-1}O_S [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over]. No coherence, Noetherian hypothesis, locally finite type or proper-support hypothesis is needed.

source.place: 0DJQ: relative Tor verification; 08CI and 08CG: bounded flat models and locality

proof.text: By compactness take finitely many opens carrying strictly perfect representatives P_j of E. If [c,d] bounds G and [a_j,b_j] bounds P_j, the local derived tensor is represented by P_j tensor G, bounded in [a_j+c,b_j+d], because P_j is termwise flat over O_X.

source.place: 0DJQ: relative Tor verification; 08CI and 08CG: bounded flat models and locality

proof.text: The affine-section definition of IsFlatOver implies stalkwise relative flatness: localize the base at f(x) and take the filtered colimit of sections on affine neighbourhoods of x; localization and filtered colimits preserve flatness. After restriction of scalars to the inverse-image structure sheaf, every term of the total complex is a summand of a finite direct sum of terms of G. The assumed relative flatness of G therefore makes every term flat over the inverse-image structure sheaf.

source.place: 0DJQ: relative Tor verification; 08CI and 08CG: bounded flat models and locality

proof.text: Choose a single interval [a,b], with a <= b, containing all the finitely many local intervals (use [0,0] for an empty cover). By 08CI each local model has Tor amplitude in [a,b]. The definition of amplitude in 08CG is cohomology vanishing after derived tensor with any module sheaf; vanishing is local, so the bound holds globally.

source.place: 0DJQ: relative Tor verification; 08CI and 08CG: bounded flat models and locality

proof.text: Represent the global derived object by a complex K, and choose a K-flat resolution of its restriction of scalars. It computes the same relative derived tensors. The uniform bound from step 3 provides the witnesses in HasFiniteTorDimensionOver. Only a proposition of existence is asserted; no arbitrary witness defines new data.

lean.statement:
theorem perfect_tensor_hasFiniteTorDimensionOver
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] (f : X ⟶ S)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : IsPerfect X E)
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hGb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, Modules.IsFlatOver (G.X n) f) :
    HasFiniteTorDimensionOver f (E ⊗ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)
